promptLines: Let \(X\) be a matrix of order \(3 \times 3\), \(Y\) be a matrix of order \(2 \times 3\) and \(Z\) be a matrix of order \(3 \times 2\). Which of the following statements are correct?
I. \((ZY)X\) is defined and is a square matrix of order 3.
II. \(Y(XZ)\) is defined and is a square matrix of order 2.
III. \(X(YZ)\) is not defined.
Select the answer using the code given below.
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

A product ​AB​ is defined only when the number of columns of ​A​ equals the number of rows of ​B​; an ​m \times n​ matrix times an ​n \times p​ matrix is ​m \times p​. I: ​ZY​ is ​(3 \times 2)(2 \times 3) = 3 \times 3​, and times ​X​ (​3 \times 3​) it is ​3 \times 3​. Correct. II: ​XZ​ is ​(3 \times 3)(3 \times 2) = 3 \times 2​, and ​Y(XZ)​ is ​(2 \times 3)(3 \times 2) = 2 \times 2​. Correct. III: ​YZ​ is ​(2 \times 3)(3 \times 2) = 2 \times 2​; ​X​ has 3 columns but ​YZ​ has 2 rows, so ​X(YZ)​ is not defined. Correct. Answer: I, II and III.

promptLines: Consider the following statements :
I. The set of all irrational numbers between \(\sqrt{12}\) and \(\sqrt{15}\) is an infinite set.
II. The set of all odd integers less than 1000 is a finite set.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Our working gives (a). Statement II turns on the word 'integers': negative odd integers make the set infinite, so II is false. A solver who reads it as positive integers would pick (c).

Statement I: between any two different real numbers there are infinitely many irrational numbers. Since ​\sqrt{12} \approx 3.46​ and ​\sqrt{15} \approx 3.87​ are different, the set is infinite. I is correct. Statement II: integers include negative numbers. The odd integers less than 1000 are ​999, 997, \ldots, 1, -1, -3, -5, \ldots​ and this list never ends on the negative side. So the set is infinite, and II is wrong. (It would be finite only if the statement said odd natural numbers.) Answer: I only.

promptLines: How many 4-digit numbers are there having all digits as odd?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The odd digits are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, which is 5 choices. Nothing says the digits must be different, so each of the four places can be filled in 5 ways independently. Also, no odd digit is zero, so the first place has no restriction. By the multiplication rule the count is ​5 \times 5 \times 5 \times 5 = 5^4 = 625​. Answer: 625.

promptLines: If \(\omega \neq 1\) is a cube root of unity, then what is \((1 + \omega - \omega^2)^{100} + (1 - \omega + \omega^2)^{100}\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Use ​1 + \omega + \omega^2 = 0​ and ​\omega^3 = 1​. Since ​1 + \omega = -\omega^2​, the first bracket is ​-\omega^2 - \omega^2 = -2\omega^2​. Since ​1 + \omega^2 = -\omega​, the second bracket is ​-\omega - \omega = -2\omega​. Now ​(-2\omega^2)^{100} = 2^{100}\omega^{200} = 2^{100}\omega^2​ because ​200 = 3 \times 66 + 2​. And ​(-2\omega)^{100} = 2^{100}\omega^{100} = 2^{100}\omega​ because ​100 = 3 \times 33 + 1​. Adding: ​2^{100}(\omega^2 + \omega) = 2^{100}(-1) = -2^{100}​. Answer: ​-2^{100}​.

promptLines: Let \(A\) and \(B\) be two square matrices of same order. If \(AB\) is a null matrix, then which one of the following is correct?

options.B: Either \(A\) or \(B\) is a null matrix
options.C: \(B\) is a null matrix if \(A\) is a non-singular matrix

questions.topicLabel: Adjoint and inverse of a matrix
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

If ​A​ is non-singular, ​A^{-1}​ exists. Multiply ​AB = O​ on the left by ​A^{-1}​: ​A^{-1}AB = A^{-1}O​, so ​B = O​. Hence (c) is always true. The others can fail. Two non-zero matrices can have a zero product, for example ​A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}​ and ​B = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}​, so (a) and (b) are wrong. And (d) fails when ​A​ is the identity matrix and ​B​ is the null matrix, since then ​A​ is not singular. Answer: ​B​ is a null matrix if ​A​ is a non-singular matrix.

promptLines: In the expansion of \((1 + x)^p (1 + x)^q\), if the coefficient of \(x^3\) is 35, then what is the value of \((p + q)\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Combine the powers: ​(1 + x)^p (1 + x)^q = (1 + x)^{p+q}​. Write ​n = p + q​. In ​(1 + x)^n​ the coefficient of ​x^3​ is ​\binom{n}{3} = \frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{6}​. Set this equal to 35: ​n(n-1)(n-2) = 210​. Try ​n = 7​: ​7 \times 6 \times 5 = 210​. It fits. So ​p + q = 7​. Answer: 7.

promptLines: If \(p\) times the \(p\)th term of an AP is equal to \(q\) times the \(q\)th term \((p \neq q)\), then what is the \((p + q)\)th term equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Let the first term be ​a​ and the common difference ​d​; the ​n​th term is ​a + (n-1)d​. Given ​p[a + (p-1)d] = q[a + (q-1)d]​. Bring everything to one side: ​a(p - q) + d(p^2 - q^2 - p + q) = 0​, that is ​a(p - q) + d(p - q)(p + q - 1) = 0​. Since ​p \neq q​, divide by ​(p - q)​: ​a + (p + q - 1)d = 0​. But the left side is exactly the ​(p + q)​th term. So it equals 0. Answer: 0.

promptLines: Let \(p = \ln(x)\), \(q = \ln(x^3)\) and \(r = \ln(x^5)\), where \(x > 1\). Which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. \(p\), \(q\) and \(r\) are in AP.
II. \(p\), \(q\) and \(r\) can never be in GP.
Select the answer using the code given below.
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Use ​\ln(x^n) = n\ln x​. Put ​t = \ln x​; since ​x > 1​, ​t > 0​. Then ​p = t​, ​q = 3t​, ​r = 5t​. I: ​q - p = 2t​ and ​r - q = 2t​, equal differences, so they are in AP. Correct. II: for a GP we need ​q^2 = pr​, that is ​9t^2 = 5t^2​, which needs ​t = 0​. But ​t > 0​, so they can never be in GP. Correct. Answer: Both I and II.

promptLines: If \(Z = \frac{1}{3}\begin{vmatrix} i & 2i & 1 \\ 2i & 3i & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 3 \end{vmatrix} = x + iy\); \(i = \sqrt{-1}\) then what is modulus of \(Z\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Expand the determinant along the first row. First term: ​i(3i \cdot 3 - 2 \cdot 1) = i(9i - 2) = -9 - 2i​. Second term: ​-2i(2i \cdot 3 - 2 \cdot 3) = -2i(6i - 6) = 12 + 12i​. Third term: ​1(2i \cdot 1 - 3i \cdot 3) = 2i - 9i = -7i​. Sum: ​(-9 + 12) + (-2 + 12 - 7)i = 3 + 3i​. So ​Z = \frac{1}{3}(3 + 3i) = 1 + i​. Its modulus is ​\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{2}​. Answer: ​\sqrt{2}​.

promptLines: What is the value of the sum \(\sum_{n=1}^{20} (i^{n-1} + i^n + i^{n+1})\) where \(i = \sqrt{-1}\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Take ​i^n​ common: ​i^{n-1} + i^n + i^{n+1} = i^n\left(\frac{1}{i} + 1 + i\right)​. Since ​\frac{1}{i} = -i​, the bracket is ​-i + 1 + i = 1​. So each term is just ​i^n​, and the sum is ​i + i^2 + \cdots + i^{20}​. Powers of ​i​ repeat every four: ​i + i^2 + i^3 + i^4 = i - 1 - i + 1 = 0​. Twenty terms make five such groups, each adding to 0. Answer: 0.

options.D: neither in AP nor in GP nor in HP

questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

​x, y, z​ in GP means ​y^2 = xz​. Take logs: ​2\ln y = \ln x + \ln z​, so ​\ln x, \ln y, \ln z​ are in AP. Adding 1 to each term of an AP keeps it an AP, so ​1 + \ln x​, ​1 + \ln y​, ​1 + \ln z​ are in AP (and all are positive because ​x, y, z > 1​). Numbers whose reciprocals are in AP are in HP by definition. So the three given fractions are in HP. Check: ​x, y, z = e, e^2, e^3​ gives ​\frac12, \frac13, \frac14​, which is an HP. Answer: in HP.

promptLines: If \(\omega = -\frac{1}{2} + i\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) then what is \(\begin{vmatrix} 1 + \omega & 1 + \omega^2 & \omega + \omega^2 \\ 1 & \omega & \omega^2 \\ \frac{1}{\omega} & \frac{1}{\omega^2} & 1 \end{vmatrix}\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

This ​\omega​ is a cube root of unity, so ​\omega^3 = 1​ and ​1 + \omega + \omega^2 = 0​. Simplify row 1: ​1 + \omega = -\omega^2​, ​1 + \omega^2 = -\omega​, ​\omega + \omega^2 = -1​. Simplify row 3: ​\frac{1}{\omega} = \omega^2​ and ​\frac{1}{\omega^2} = \omega​, so row 3 is ​(\omega^2, \omega, 1)​. Row 1 is therefore ​(-\omega^2, -\omega, -1)​, which is ​-1​ times row 3. When one row is a multiple of another, the determinant is zero. Answer: 0.

promptLines: If the sum of the first \(n\) terms of a series is \(n(2n + 1)\), then what is the \(n\)th term?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The ​n​th term is the sum of ​n​ terms minus the sum of ​(n-1)​ terms: ​T_n = S_n - S_{n-1}​. Here ​S_n = 2n^2 + n​ and ​S_{n-1} = 2(n-1)^2 + (n-1) = 2n^2 - 4n + 2 + n - 1 = 2n^2 - 3n + 1​. Subtract: ​T_n = (2n^2 + n) - (2n^2 - 3n + 1) = 4n - 1​. Check: ​T_1 = 3 = S_1 = 1 \times 3​. Correct. Answer: ​4n - 1​.

promptLines: In how many ways can the letters of the word INDIA be permutated such that in each combination, vowels should occupy odd positions?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

INDIA has 5 letters: vowels I, I, A (three, with I repeated) and consonants N, D (two). The odd positions are 1st, 3rd and 5th, exactly three places, so the three vowels fill them and the consonants take the 2nd and 4th places. Vowels: arrangements of I, I, A are ​\frac{3!}{2!} = 3​. Consonants: N and D can be arranged in ​2! = 2​ ways. Total ​= 3 \times 2 = 6​. Answer: 6.

promptLines: The letters of the word EQUATION are arranged in such a way that all vowels as well as consonants are together. How many such arrangements are there?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

EQUATION has 8 different letters: vowels E, U, A, I, O (five) and consonants Q, T, N (three). Tie the vowels into one block and the consonants into another block. The two blocks can be placed in ​2! = 2​ orders. Inside the vowel block the letters can be arranged in ​5! = 120​ ways, and inside the consonant block in ​3! = 6​ ways. Total ​= 2 \times 120 \times 6 = 1440​. Answer: 1440.

promptLines: If \(n\) is a root of the equation \(x^2 + px + m = 0\) and \(m\) is a root of the equation \(x^2 + px + n = 0\), where \(m \neq n\), then what is the value of \(p + m + n\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

A root satisfies its equation. So ​n^2 + pn + m = 0​ and ​m^2 + pm + n = 0​. Subtract the second from the first: ​(n^2 - m^2) + p(n - m) - (n - m) = 0​. Factor out ​(n - m)​: ​(n - m)(n + m + p - 1) = 0​. Since ​m \neq n​, the first factor is not zero, so ​n + m + p - 1 = 0​, giving ​p + m + n = 1​. Answer: 1.

promptLines: In how many ways can a student choose \((n - 2)\) courses out of \(n\) courses if 2 courses are compulsory \((n > 4)\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The 2 compulsory courses are taken for sure. That leaves ​(n - 2) - 2 = n - 4​ courses still to be chosen, from the remaining ​n - 2​ courses. The number of ways is ​\binom{n-2}{n-4}​. Using ​\binom{N}{r} = \binom{N}{N-r}​, this equals ​\binom{n-2}{2} = \frac{(n-2)(n-3)}{2}​. Check with ​n = 5​: choose 1 more course from 3, which is 3 ways, and the formula gives ​\frac{3 \times 2}{2} = 3​. Answer: ​(n - 2)(n - 3)/2​.

promptLines: If \(D_n = \begin{vmatrix} n & 20 & 30 \\ n^2 & 40 & 50 \\ n^3 & 60 & 70 \end{vmatrix}\) then what is the value of \(\sum_{n=1}^{4} D_n\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Only the first column changes with ​n​, so the determinants can be added by adding their first columns. ​\sum n = 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10​, ​\sum n^2 = 1 + 4 + 9 + 16 = 30​, ​\sum n^3 = 1 + 8 + 27 + 64 = 100​. So the sum is ​\begin{vmatrix} 10 & 20 & 30 \\ 30 & 40 & 50 \\ 100 & 60 & 70 \end{vmatrix}​. Expand along row 1: ​10(2800 - 3000) - 20(2100 - 5000) + 30(1800 - 4000) = -2000 + 58000 - 66000 = -10000​. Answer: ​-10000​.

promptLines: Consider the following in respect of the matrices \(P = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & c & -b \\ -c & 0 & a \\ b & -a & 0 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(Q = \begin{bmatrix} a^2 & ab & ac \\ ab & b^2 & bc \\ ac & bc & c^2 \end{bmatrix}\)
I. \(PQ\) is a null matrix.
II. \(QP\) is an identity matrix of order 3.
III. \(PQ = QP\) Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Multiply row 1 of ​P​, ​(0, c, -b)​, by the columns of ​Q​: ​c \cdot ab - b \cdot ac = 0​, ​c \cdot b^2 - b \cdot bc = 0​, ​c \cdot bc - b \cdot c^2 = 0​. Rows 2 and 3 give zeros in the same way (for example ​-c \cdot a^2 + a \cdot ac = 0​). So ​PQ = O​ and I is correct. For ​QP​: row 1 of ​Q​, ​(a^2, ab, ac)​, times column 1 of ​P​, ​(0, -c, b)​, gives ​-abc + abc = 0​, and every other entry also cancels, so ​QP = O​ too. Hence II is wrong (it is not the identity) and III is correct since ​PQ = QP = O​. Answer: I and III.

promptLines: If \(P\) is a skew-symmetric matrix of order 3, then what is \(\det(P)\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Skew-symmetric means ​P^T = -P​. Take determinants of both sides. ​\det(P^T) = \det(P)​, and for a ​3 \times 3​ matrix ​\det(-P) = (-1)^3\det(P) = -\det(P)​. So ​\det(P) = -\det(P)​, which gives ​2\det(P) = 0​ and ​\det(P) = 0​. This holds for every skew-symmetric matrix of odd order. Answer: 0.

promptLines: If \(4\sin^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}x = \pi\), then what is \(\sin^{-1}x + 4\cos^{-1}x\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Use the identity ​\sin^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}x = \frac{\pi}{2}​. Write the given equation as ​3\sin^{-1}x + (\sin^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}x) = \pi​, so ​3\sin^{-1}x = \pi - \frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{\pi}{2}​ and ​\sin^{-1}x = \frac{\pi}{6}​. Then ​\cos^{-1}x = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3}​. Required value ​= \frac{\pi}{6} + 4 \cdot \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{8\pi}{6} = \frac{9\pi}{6} = \frac{3\pi}{2}​. Quicker: the two expressions add up to ​5 \cdot \frac{\pi}{2}​, so the second is ​\frac{5\pi}{2} - \pi = \frac{3\pi}{2}​. Answer: ​3\pi/2​.

promptLines: What is \(\cot^2(\sec^{-1}2) + \tan^2(\mathrm{cosec}^{-1}3)\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Let ​\theta = \sec^{-1}2​, so ​\sec\theta = 2​. Then ​\tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta - 1 = 4 - 1 = 3​, so ​\cot^2\theta = \frac{1}{3}​. Let ​\phi = \mathrm{cosec}^{-1}3​, so ​\mathrm{cosec}\,\phi = 3​. Then ​\cot^2\phi = \mathrm{cosec}^2\phi - 1 = 9 - 1 = 8​, so ​\tan^2\phi = \frac{1}{8}​. Adding: ​\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{8} = \frac{8 + 3}{24} = \frac{11}{24}​. Answer: 11/24.

promptLines: In a triangle \(ABC\) \(\frac{a}{\cos A} = \frac{b}{\cos B} = \frac{c}{\cos C}\) What is the area of the triangle if \(a = 6\) cm?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

By the sine rule, ​a = 2R\sin A​, ​b = 2R\sin B​, ​c = 2R\sin C​. Put these in the given relation: ​\frac{2R\sin A}{\cos A} = \frac{2R\sin B}{\cos B} = \frac{2R\sin C}{\cos C}​, so ​\tan A = \tan B = \tan C​. Angles of a triangle lie between ​0^\circ​ and ​180^\circ​, where equal tangents mean equal angles. So ​A = B = C = 60^\circ​ and the triangle is equilateral with side 6 cm. Area ​= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 6^2 = 9\sqrt{3}​ square cm. Answer: ​9\sqrt{3}​ square cm.

promptLines: The roots of the equation \(7x^2 - 6x + 1 = 0\) are \(\tan\alpha\) and \(\tan\beta\), where \(2\alpha\) and \(2\beta\) are the angles of a triangle.
Which one of the following is correct?

options.B: The triangle is isosceles but not right-angled

questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Sum of roots: ​\tan\alpha + \tan\beta = \frac{6}{7}​. Product: ​\tan\alpha\tan\beta = \frac{1}{7}​. So ​\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \frac{6/7}{1 - 1/7} = 1​, giving ​\alpha + \beta = 45^\circ​ (both are acute since ​2\alpha, 2\beta < 180^\circ​). Then ​2\alpha + 2\beta = 90^\circ​, so the third angle is ​180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ​: the triangle is right-angled. Is it isosceles? The discriminant ​36 - 28 = 8​ is not zero, so ​\tan\alpha \neq \tan\beta​ and the two acute angles are different. So it is right-angled but not isosceles. Answer: The triangle is right-angled.

promptLines: In a triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle A = 75^\circ\) and \(\angle B = 45^\circ\). What is \(2a - b\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

​C = 180^\circ - 75^\circ - 45^\circ = 60^\circ​. By the sine rule, ​a = k\sin 75^\circ​, ​b = k\sin 45^\circ​, ​c = k\sin 60^\circ​. Now ​\sin 75^\circ = \sin(45^\circ + 30^\circ) = \frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4}​. So ​2a - b = k\left(\frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{2} - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = \frac{k\sqrt{6}}{2}​. And ​c = \frac{k\sqrt{3}}{2}​. Dividing: ​\frac{2a - b}{c} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{2}​. So ​2a - b = \sqrt{2}c​. Answer: ​\sqrt{2}c​.

promptLines: What is the number of solutions of the equation \(\cot 2x \cdot \cot 3x = 1\) for \(0 < x < \pi\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Our working gives (none). Faulty as printed. cos 5x = 0 gives five values in (0, pi), but x = pi/2 makes cot 2x = cot(pi) undefined, so only four are valid solutions (checked numerically) and 4 is not an option. The setter almost certainly intended (c) 'Only five'.

Write the equation as ​\cos 2x\cos 3x = \sin 2x\sin 3x​, so ​\cos 2x\cos 3x - \sin 2x\sin 3x = 0​, that is ​\cos 5x = 0​. Then ​5x = \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{2}, \frac{5\pi}{2}, \frac{7\pi}{2}, \frac{9\pi}{2}​, giving ​x = \frac{\pi}{10}, \frac{3\pi}{10}, \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{7\pi}{10}, \frac{9\pi}{10}​ in the interval. This count of five is what the setter intended, option (c). Strictly, though, at ​x = \frac{\pi}{2}​ we get ​\cot 2x = \cot\pi​, which is not defined, so that value must be thrown out. The other four values do satisfy the equation, so the true number of solutions is 4, which is not among the options.

promptLines: What is the general solution of \(\cos^{100}x - \sin^{100}x = 1\)? where \(n\) is an integer.
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Rewrite as ​\cos^{100}x = 1 + \sin^{100}x​. Even powers are never negative, so the right side is at least 1. But ​\cos^{100}x​ is at most 1, because ​|\cos x| \leq 1​. Both can hold only when ​\cos^{100}x = 1​ and ​\sin^{100}x = 0​, that is ​\sin x = 0​ (then ​\cos x = \pm 1​ automatically). ​\sin x = 0​ gives ​x = n\pi​. Options (b) and (c) each give only half of these solutions. Answer: ​n\pi​.

promptLines: In a triangle \(ABC\) \(\tan A + \tan B + \tan C = k\) What is the value of \(\cot A\cot B\cot C\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

In a triangle ​A + B = 180^\circ - C​, so ​\tan(A + B) = -\tan C​. Expand: ​\frac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A\tan B} = -\tan C​. Cross-multiply: ​\tan A + \tan B = -\tan C + \tan A\tan B\tan C​. So ​\tan A + \tan B + \tan C = \tan A\tan B\tan C​. Hence ​\tan A\tan B\tan C = k​, and taking the reciprocal, ​\cot A\cot B\cot C = \frac{1}{k}​. Check with the equilateral triangle: ​k = 3\sqrt{3}​ and ​\cot^3 60^\circ = \frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}}​. Answer: ​1/k​.

promptLines: What is \(\sin 12^\circ \sin 48^\circ\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Use ​2\sin A\sin B = \cos(A - B) - \cos(A + B)​. So ​\sin 12^\circ\sin 48^\circ = \frac{1}{2}\left[\cos 36^\circ - \cos 60^\circ\right]​. The standard value is ​\cos 36^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{5} + 1}{4}​, and ​\cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}​. So the bracket is ​\frac{\sqrt{5} + 1}{4} - \frac{2}{4} = \frac{\sqrt{5} - 1}{4}​. Half of that is ​\frac{\sqrt{5} - 1}{8}​. Rough check: ​0.208 \times 0.743 \approx 0.155​ and ​\frac{2.236 - 1}{8} \approx 0.155​. Answer: ​\frac{\sqrt{5} - 1}{8}​.

promptLines: What is \(\frac{\cos 17^\circ - \sin 17^\circ}{\cos 17^\circ + \sin 17^\circ}\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Divide the top and bottom by ​\cos 17^\circ​: the expression becomes ​\frac{1 - \tan 17^\circ}{1 + \tan 17^\circ}​. Since ​\tan 45^\circ = 1​, this is ​\frac{\tan 45^\circ - \tan 17^\circ}{1 + \tan 45^\circ\tan 17^\circ} = \tan(45^\circ - 17^\circ) = \tan 28^\circ​. Now ​\tan 28^\circ = \cot(90^\circ - 28^\circ) = \cot 62^\circ​. Answer: ​\cot 62^\circ​.

promptLines: Consider the following numbers :
I. \(\tan 22 \cdot 5^\circ\)
II. \(\cot 22 \cdot 5^\circ\)
III. \(\tan 22 \cdot 5^\circ - \cot 22 \cdot 5^\circ\) How many of the above are irrational numbers?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Here ​22 \cdot 5^\circ​ means ​22.5^\circ​, half of ​45^\circ​. Use ​\tan\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{1 - \cos\theta}{\sin\theta}​ with ​\theta = 45^\circ​: ​\tan 22.5^\circ = \frac{1 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} = \sqrt{2} - 1​, which is irrational. Its reciprocal is ​\cot 22.5^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} - 1} = \sqrt{2} + 1​, also irrational. Their difference is ​(\sqrt{2} - 1) - (\sqrt{2} + 1) = -2​, which is rational. So exactly two of the three numbers are irrational. Answer: Only two.

promptLines: If \(\frac{x}{\cos\theta} = \frac{y}{\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} - \theta\right)} = \frac{z}{\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} + \theta\right)}\) then what is \(x + y + z\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Let each ratio equal ​k​. Then ​x = k\cos\theta​, ​y = k\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} - \theta\right)​, ​z = k\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} + \theta\right)​. Use ​\cos(A - B) + \cos(A + B) = 2\cos A\cos B​ with ​A = \frac{2\pi}{3}​: ​y + z = 2k\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}\cos\theta = 2k\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\cos\theta = -k\cos\theta​. Therefore ​x + y + z = k\cos\theta - k\cos\theta = 0​. Answer: 0.

promptLines: If \(p\tan(\theta - 30^\circ) = q\tan(\theta + 120^\circ)\), then what is \((p + q)/(p - q)\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Write ​A = \theta + 120^\circ​ and ​B = \theta - 30^\circ​. The given relation is ​\frac{p}{q} = \frac{\tan A}{\tan B}​. By componendo and dividendo, ​\frac{p + q}{p - q} = \frac{\tan A + \tan B}{\tan A - \tan B}​. Writing tan as sin over cos, this equals ​\frac{\sin A\cos B + \cos A\sin B}{\sin A\cos B - \cos A\sin B} = \frac{\sin(A + B)}{\sin(A - B)}​. Here ​A + B = 2\theta + 90^\circ​ and ​A - B = 150^\circ​. So the value is ​\frac{\sin(2\theta + 90^\circ)}{\sin 150^\circ} = \frac{\cos 2\theta}{1/2} = 2\cos 2\theta​. Answer: ​2\cos 2\theta​.

promptLines: Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be two non-void relations on a set \(A\). Which of the following statements are correct?
I. \(P\) and \(Q\) are reflexive \(\Rightarrow P \cap Q\) is reflexive.
II. \(P\) and \(Q\) are symmetric \(\Rightarrow P \cup Q\) is symmetric.
III. \(P\) and \(Q\) are transitive \(\Rightarrow P \cap Q\) is transitive.
Select the answer using the code given below.
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

I: if both are reflexive, every pair ​(a, a)​ is in ​P​ and in ​Q​, so it is in ​P \cap Q​. Correct. II: take ​(a, b)​ in ​P \cup Q​. It lies in ​P​ or in ​Q​; that relation is symmetric, so ​(b, a)​ lies in it too, and hence in ​P \cup Q​. Correct. III: take ​(a, b)​ and ​(b, c)​ in ​P \cap Q​. Both pairs are in ​P​, so ​(a, c)​ is in ​P​; both are in ​Q​, so ​(a, c)​ is in ​Q​. So ​(a, c)​ is in ​P \cap Q​. Correct. (Only the union of transitive relations can fail, and that is not asked.) Answer: I, II and III.

promptLines: If \(A\) and \(B\) are two non-empty sets having 10 elements in common, then how many elements do \(A \times B\) and \(B \times A\) have in common?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

A pair ​(x, y)​ is in ​A \times B​ when ​x​ is in ​A​ and ​y​ is in ​B​. It is in ​B \times A​ when ​x​ is in ​B​ and ​y​ is in ​A​. For the pair to be in both, ​x​ must be in both ​A​ and ​B​, and ​y​ must be in both ​A​ and ​B​. So ​(A \times B) \cap (B \times A) = (A \cap B) \times (A \cap B)​. With ​n(A \cap B) = 10​, the number of common pairs is ​10 \times 10 = 100​. Answer: 100.

promptLines: What is the remainder when \(7^n - 6n\) is divided by 36 for \(n = 100\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Write ​7 = 1 + 6​ and use the binomial theorem: ​7^n = (1 + 6)^n = 1 + 6n + \binom{n}{2}6^2 + \binom{n}{3}6^3 + \cdots​. Every term from the third onwards contains ​6^2 = 36​ as a factor. So ​7^n - 6n = 1 + 36 \times (\text{an integer})​. This is true for every positive integer ​n​, including ​n = 100​. Check with ​n = 2​: ​49 - 12 = 37 = 36 + 1​. So the remainder is 1. Answer: 1.

promptLines: What is the maximum number of possible points of intersection of four straight lines and a circle (intersection is between lines as well as circle and lines)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Count the two kinds of intersection separately. Lines with lines: two straight lines meet in at most one point, and 4 lines form ​\binom{4}{2} = 6​ pairs, so at most 6 points. Lines with the circle: one line cuts a circle in at most 2 points, so 4 lines give at most ​4 \times 2 = 8​ points. The maximum happens when all these points are different, giving ​6 + 8 = 14​. Answer: 14.

promptLines: In an AP, the ratio of the sum of the first \(p\) terms to the sum of the first \(q\) terms is \(p^2 : q^2\).
Which one of the following is correct?

options.A: The first term is equal to the common difference
options.B: The first term is equal to twice the common difference
options.C: The common difference is equal to twice the first term
options.D: The first term is equal to square of the common difference

questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

With first term ​a​ and common difference ​d​, ​S_n = \frac{n}{2}[2a + (n-1)d]​. The condition gives ​\frac{p[2a + (p-1)d]}{q[2a + (q-1)d]} = \frac{p^2}{q^2}​, so ​\frac{2a + (p-1)d}{2a + (q-1)d} = \frac{p}{q}​. Cross-multiply: ​2aq + (p-1)qd = 2ap + (q-1)pd​. Then ​2a(q - p) = d[(q-1)p - (p-1)q] = d(q - p)​. For ​p \neq q​ this gives ​d = 2a​. Check: ​1, 3, 5, \ldots​ has ​S_n = n^2​. Answer: The common difference is equal to twice the first term.

promptLines: What is the number of real roots of the equation \((x - 1)^2 + (x - 3)^2 + (x - 5)^2 = 0\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

For real ​x​ each square is zero or positive. A sum of three such squares can be zero only if every one is zero at the same time. That would need ​x = 1​, ​x = 3​ and ​x = 5​ together, which is impossible. So no real ​x​ works. Check by expanding: ​3x^2 - 18x + 35 = 0​ has discriminant ​18^2 - 4 \times 3 \times 35 = 324 - 420 = -96 < 0​, so no real roots. Answer: None.

promptLines: In a class of 240 students, 180 passed in English, 130 passed in Hindi and 150 passed in Sanskrit. Further, 60 passed in only one subject, 110 passed in only two subjects and 10 passed in none of the subjects. How many passed in all three subjects?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Students who passed at least one subject: ​240 - 10 = 230​. Each of them passed exactly one, exactly two or all three subjects. Let ​x​ pass all three. Then ​60 + 110 + x = 230​, so ​x = 60​. Check with the subject totals: adding ​180 + 130 + 150 = 460​ counts a one-subject student once, a two-subject student twice and a three-subject student three times: ​60 + 2 \times 110 + 3 \times 60 = 460​. It matches. Answer: 60.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \(Z_1\) and \(Z_2\) be any two complex numbers such that \(Z_1^2 + Z_2^2 + Z_1Z_2 = 0\).
What is the value of \(\left|\frac{Z_1}{Z_2}\right|\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Divide the given relation by ​Z_2^2​ (taking ​Z_2 \neq 0​) and put ​t = \frac{Z_1}{Z_2}​: ​t^2 + t + 1 = 0​. Multiply by ​(t - 1)​: ​t^3 - 1 = 0​, so ​t^3 = 1​ with ​t \neq 1​. That means ​t​ is a complex cube root of unity, ​\omega​ or ​\omega^2​, that is ​t = \frac{-1 \pm i\sqrt{3}}{2}​. Its modulus is ​\sqrt{\frac{1}{4} + \frac{3}{4}} = 1​. (Also directly: ​|t|^3 = |t^3| = 1​ gives ​|t| = 1​.) Answer: 1.

promptLines: What is the value of \(\frac{1}{2} + \mathrm{Re}\left(\frac{Z_1}{Z_2}\right)\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Divide the given relation by ​Z_2^2​ and put ​t = \frac{Z_1}{Z_2}​: ​t^2 + t + 1 = 0​. By the quadratic formula, ​t = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1 - 4}}{2} = \frac{-1 \pm i\sqrt{3}}{2}​. For either sign the real part is ​-\frac{1}{2}​. So ​\frac{1}{2} + \mathrm{Re}\left(\frac{Z_1}{Z_2}\right) = \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{2} = 0​. Answer: 0.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : The product of 5 consecutive terms of an AP is 229635. The first, second and fifth terms are in GP.
What is the common difference?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Let the terms be ​a, a + d, a + 2d, a + 3d, a + 4d​. First, second and fifth in GP: ​(a + d)^2 = a(a + 4d)​, so ​a^2 + 2ad + d^2 = a^2 + 4ad​, giving ​d^2 = 2ad​ and ​d = 2a​ (taking ​d \neq 0​). The terms become ​a, 3a, 5a, 7a, 9a​. Their product is ​945a^5 = 229635​, so ​a^5 = 243 = 3^5​ and ​a = 3​. Hence ​d = 2a = 6​. The terms are ​3, 9, 15, 21, 27​; check: ​3, 9, 27​ are in GP. Answer: 6.

promptLines: What is the sum of all five terms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Let the terms be ​a, a + d, a + 2d, a + 3d, a + 4d​. The GP condition ​(a + d)^2 = a(a + 4d)​ gives ​d^2 = 2ad​, so ​d = 2a​ (for ​d \neq 0​). The terms are then ​a, 3a, 5a, 7a, 9a​, with product ​1 \times 3 \times 5 \times 7 \times 9 \times a^5 = 945a^5​. Setting ​945a^5 = 229635​ gives ​a^5 = 243​, so ​a = 3​. The terms are ​3, 9, 15, 21, 27​. Their sum is ​25a = 75​. Answer: 75.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \((8 + 3\sqrt{7})^{20} = U + V\) and \((8 - 3\sqrt{7})^{20} = W\), where \(U\) is an integer and \(0 < V < 1\).
What is \(V + W\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Add the two binomial expansions. In ​(8 + 3\sqrt{7})^{20} + (8 - 3\sqrt{7})^{20}​ the terms with odd powers of ​\sqrt{7}​ cancel and the rest are whole numbers, so ​U + V + W​ is an integer. Since ​U​ is an integer, ​V + W​ is an integer too. Now ​3\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{63} \approx 7.94​, so ​8 - 3\sqrt{7} \approx 0.06​ lies between 0 and 1, and so does its 20th power: ​0 < W < 1​. With ​0 < V < 1​ we get ​0 < V + W < 2​. The only integer in that range is 1. Answer: 1.

promptLines: What is the value of \((U + V)W\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

​(U + V)W​ is simply the product of the two given powers: ​(8 + 3\sqrt{7})^{20}(8 - 3\sqrt{7})^{20} = \left[(8 + 3\sqrt{7})(8 - 3\sqrt{7})\right]^{20}​. Use ​(a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2​: ​8^2 - (3\sqrt{7})^2 = 64 - 63 = 1​. So the value is ​1^{20} = 1​. Answer: 1.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : The roots of the quadratic equation \(a^2(b^2 - c^2)x^2 + b^2(c^2 - a^2)x + c^2(a^2 - b^2) = 0\) are equal \((a^2 \neq b^2 \neq c^2)\).
Which one of the following statements is correct?

options.D: \(a^2\), \(b^2\), \(c^2\) are neither in AP nor in GP nor in HP.

questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Add the three coefficients: ​a^2(b^2 - c^2) + b^2(c^2 - a^2) + c^2(a^2 - b^2) = 0​. So ​x = 1​ satisfies the equation. The roots are equal, so both roots are 1 and their product is 1: ​\frac{c^2(a^2 - b^2)}{a^2(b^2 - c^2)} = 1​. Cross-multiply: ​a^2c^2 - b^2c^2 = a^2b^2 - a^2c^2​, so ​2a^2c^2 = b^2(a^2 + c^2)​, that is ​b^2 = \frac{2a^2c^2}{a^2 + c^2}​. This says ​b^2​ is the harmonic mean of ​a^2​ and ​c^2​. Answer: ​a^2​, ​b^2​, ​c^2​ are in HP.

promptLines: Which one of the following is a root of the equation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

For ​Ax^2 + Bx + C = 0​ with equal roots, each root is ​-\frac{B}{2A}​ (half the sum of the roots). Here ​A = a^2(b^2 - c^2)​ and ​B = b^2(c^2 - a^2)​. So the root is ​-\frac{b^2(c^2 - a^2)}{2a^2(b^2 - c^2)}​. Take the minus sign into the bottom bracket: ​\frac{b^2(c^2 - a^2)}{2a^2(c^2 - b^2)}​. (Its value is 1, since the coefficients add up to zero.) Answer: ​\frac{b^2(c^2 - a^2)}{2a^2(c^2 - b^2)}​.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -3 & 4 \\ 2 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\)
What is \(A(\mathrm{adj}\, A)\) equal to?
questions.topicLabel: Adjoint and inverse of a matrix
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Use the property ​A(\mathrm{adj}\, A) = |A| I​. So only the determinant is needed. Expand along the first row: ​|A| = 3[(-3)(1) - (4)(-1)] - (-3)[(2)(1) - (4)(0)] + 4[(2)(-1) - (-3)(0)] = 3(1) + 3(2) + 4(-2) = 3 + 6 - 8 = 1​. Hence ​A(\mathrm{adj}\, A) = 1 \cdot I​, the identity matrix of order 3. Answer: the identity matrix, option (d).

promptLines: What is \(A^{-1}\) equal to?
questions.topicLabel: Adjoint and inverse of a matrix
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

​A^{-1} = \frac{\mathrm{adj}\, A}{|A|}​. Expanding along row 1, ​|A| = 3(-3 + 4) + 3(2 - 0) + 4(-2 - 0) = 1​. So ​A^{-1} = \mathrm{adj}\, A​. Cofactors: row 1 gives ​1, -2, -2​; row 2 gives ​-1, 3, 3​; row 3 gives ​0, -4, -3​. The adjoint is the transpose of the cofactor matrix: ​\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & -4 \\ -2 & 3 & -3 \end{bmatrix}​. Check its first row against column 1 of ​A​: ​1(3) - 1(2) + 0 = 1​. Correct. The other options are this matrix divided by 2, multiplied by 2, or divided by 5. Answer: option (a).

promptLines: What is \(3\alpha + 2\beta\) equal to if \((2\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + 27\hat{k}) \times (\hat{i} + \alpha\hat{j} + \beta\hat{k})\) is a null vector?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The cross product of two non-zero vectors is the null vector only when the vectors are parallel, which means their components are proportional: ​\frac{2}{1} = \frac{6}{\alpha} = \frac{27}{\beta}​. From ​\frac{6}{\alpha} = 2​ we get ​\alpha = 3​. From ​\frac{27}{\beta} = 2​ we get ​\beta = \frac{27}{2}​. So ​3\alpha + 2\beta = 9 + 27 = 36​. Answer: 36.

promptLines: For what value of the angle between the vectors \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) is the quantity \(|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}| + \sqrt{3}|\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}|\) maximum?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Our working gives (b). Because of the modulus on the dot product, 150 degrees gives the same maximum; only 30 degrees is among the options.

Let the angle be ​\theta​. Then ​|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}| = |\vec{a}||\vec{b}|\sin\theta​ and ​|\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}| = |\vec{a}||\vec{b}||\cos\theta|​. For the angles in the options ​\cos\theta​ is positive, so the quantity is ​|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|(\sin\theta + \sqrt{3}\cos\theta)​. Write ​\sin\theta + \sqrt{3}\cos\theta = 2\left(\frac{1}{2}\sin\theta + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos\theta\right) = 2\sin(\theta + 60^\circ)​. This is largest, equal to 2, when ​\theta + 60^\circ = 90^\circ​, that is ​\theta = 30^\circ​. Check: at ​30^\circ​, ​\frac{1}{2} + \sqrt{3} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 2​. Answer: ​30^\circ​.

promptLines: Let \(\theta\) be the angle between two unit vectors \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\). If \(\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}\) is perpendicular to \(5\vec{a} - 4\vec{b}\), then what is \(\cos\theta + \cos 2\theta\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero: ​(\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}) \cdot (5\vec{a} - 4\vec{b}) = 0​. Expand: ​5|\vec{a}|^2 - 4\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + 10\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} - 8|\vec{b}|^2 = 0​. For unit vectors ​|\vec{a}|^2 = |\vec{b}|^2 = 1​ and ​\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = \cos\theta​. So ​5 + 6\cos\theta - 8 = 0​, giving ​\cos\theta = \frac{1}{2}​. Then ​\cos 2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 = \frac{1}{2} - 1 = -\frac{1}{2}​. Sum: ​\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{2} = 0​. Answer: 0.

promptLines: Let \(ABCDEF\) be a regular hexagon. If \(\overrightarrow{AD} = m\overrightarrow{BC}\) and \(\overrightarrow{CF} = n\overrightarrow{AB}\), then what is \(mn\) equal to?
questions.topicLabel: Vectors at work: force, moment and geometry
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Place the hexagon with centre at the origin and side 1: ​A(1, 0)​, ​B\left(\frac12, \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)​, ​C\left(-\frac12, \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)​, ​D(-1, 0)​, ​F\left(\frac12, -\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)​. Then ​\overrightarrow{AD} = (-2, 0)​ and ​\overrightarrow{BC} = (-1, 0)​, so ​\overrightarrow{AD} = 2\overrightarrow{BC}​ and ​m = 2​. Next ​\overrightarrow{CF} = (1, -\sqrt{3})​ and ​\overrightarrow{AB} = \left(-\frac12, \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)​, so ​\overrightarrow{CF} = -2\overrightarrow{AB}​ and ​n = -2​. (A long diagonal is parallel to a side and twice as long; here ​CF​ points opposite to ​AB​.) So ​mn = 2 \times (-2) = -4​. Answer: ​-4​.

promptLines: The vectors \(\vec{a}\), \(\vec{b}\) and \(\vec{c}\) are of the same length. If taken pairwise, they form equal angles. If \(\vec{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j}\) and \(\vec{b} = \hat{j} + \hat{k}\), then what can \(\vec{c}\) be equal to?
I. \(\hat{i} + \hat{k}\)
II. \(\frac{-\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - \hat{k}}{3}\) Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

​|\vec{a}| = |\vec{b}| = \sqrt{2}​ and ​\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 1​. Since all lengths are equal, equal angles mean equal dot products. So ​\vec{c}​ must satisfy ​|\vec{c}| = \sqrt{2}​, ​\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 1​ and ​\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} = 1​. Test I: ​\vec{c} = (1, 0, 1)​ has length ​\sqrt{2}​, ​\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 1​, ​\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} = 1​. It works. Test II: ​\vec{c} = \frac{1}{3}(-1, 4, -1)​ has ​|\vec{c}|^2 = \frac{1 + 16 + 1}{9} = 2​, ​\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = \frac{-1 + 4}{3} = 1​, ​\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} = \frac{4 - 1}{3} = 1​. It works too. Answer: Both I and II.

promptLines: The diagonals of a quadrilateral \(ABCD\) are along the lines \(x - 2y = 1\) and \(4x + 2y = 3\). The quadrilateral \(ABCD\) may be a
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Our working gives (d). The wording 'may be' is loose: a square (which is a rectangle and a parallelogram) and some cyclic quadrilaterals also have perpendicular diagonals. Rhombus is the clearly intended answer.

Find the slopes. ​x - 2y = 1​ gives ​y = \frac{x - 1}{2}​, slope ​\frac{1}{2}​. ​4x + 2y = 3​ gives ​y = -2x + \frac{3}{2}​, slope ​-2​. The product of the slopes is ​\frac{1}{2} \times (-2) = -1​, so the diagonals are perpendicular. Among the named shapes, the one whose defining feature is perpendicular diagonals is the rhombus (its diagonals bisect each other at right angles). A general rectangle or parallelogram does not have perpendicular diagonals. Answer: rhombus.

promptLines: The foci of the ellipse \(4x^2 + 9y^2 = 1\) are at \(Q\) and \(R\). If \(P(x, y)\) is any point on the ellipse, then what is \(PQ + PR\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

For any point on an ellipse, the sum of its distances from the two foci equals the length of the major axis, ​2a​. Write the equation in standard form: ​\frac{x^2}{1/4} + \frac{y^2}{1/9} = 1​. So ​a^2 = \frac{1}{4}​ (the larger one) and ​b^2 = \frac{1}{9}​, giving ​a = \frac{1}{2}​. Hence ​PQ + PR = 2a = 2 \times \frac{1}{2} = 1​. Answer: 1.

promptLines: If \(P(2, 4)\), \(Q(8, 12)\), \(R(10, 14)\) and \(S(x, y)\) are vertices of a parallelogram, then what is \((x + y)\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Our working gives (b). Taken in the order P, Q, R, S. The other possible fourth vertices, (0, 2) and (16, 22), give sums 2 and 38, which are not among the options.

In a parallelogram ​PQRS​ the diagonals ​PR​ and ​QS​ bisect each other, so they have the same midpoint. Midpoint of ​PR​: ​\left(\frac{2 + 10}{2}, \frac{4 + 14}{2}\right) = (6, 9)​. Midpoint of ​QS​: ​\left(\frac{8 + x}{2}, \frac{12 + y}{2}\right)​. Equate: ​8 + x = 12​ gives ​x = 4​, and ​12 + y = 18​ gives ​y = 6​. So ​S = (4, 6)​ and ​x + y = 10​. Answer: 10.

promptLines: The equation of a circle is \((x^2 - 4x + 3) + (y^2 - 6y + 8) = 0\) Which of the following statements are correct?
I. The end points of a diameter of the circle are at \((1, 2)\) and \((3, 4)\).
II. The end points of a diameter of the circle are at \((1, 4)\) and \((3, 2)\).
III. The end points of a diameter of the circle are at \((2, 4)\) and \((4, 2)\).
Select the answer using the code given below.
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Complete the squares: ​(x - 2)^2 - 1 + (y - 3)^2 - 1 = 0​, so ​(x - 2)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 2​. Centre ​(2, 3)​, radius ​\sqrt{2}​. The ends of a diameter must lie on the circle and have the centre as midpoint. I: midpoint of ​(1, 2)​ and ​(3, 4)​ is ​(2, 3)​, and ​(1, 2)​ is on the circle since ​1 + 1 = 2​. Correct. II: midpoint of ​(1, 4)​ and ​(3, 2)​ is ​(2, 3)​, and ​1 + 1 = 2​. Correct. III: midpoint of ​(2, 4)​ and ​(4, 2)​ is ​(3, 3)​, not the centre. Wrong. Answer: I and II only.

promptLines: Consider the points \(P(4k, 4k)\) and \(Q(4k, -4k)\) lying on the parabola \(y^2 = 4kx\). If the vertex is \(A\), then what is \(\angle PAQ\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The vertex of ​y^2 = 4kx​ is the origin, so ​A = (0, 0)​. Slope of ​AP = \frac{4k - 0}{4k - 0} = 1​. Slope of ​AQ = \frac{-4k - 0}{4k - 0} = -1​. The product of the slopes is ​1 \times (-1) = -1​, so ​AP​ is perpendicular to ​AQ​. In other words, ​AP​ makes ​45^\circ​ above the axis and ​AQ​ makes ​45^\circ​ below it. So ​\angle PAQ = 90^\circ​. Answer: ​90^\circ​.

promptLines: Direction :

Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : A triangle \(ABC\) is inscribed in the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 100\). \(B\) and \(C\) have coordinates \((6, 8)\) and \((-8, 6)\) respectively.
What is \(\angle BAC\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The centre is ​O(0, 0)​. Slope of ​OB = \frac{8}{6} = \frac{4}{3}​ and slope of ​OC = \frac{6}{-8} = -\frac{3}{4}​. Their product is ​-1​, so ​\angle BOC = 90^\circ​: the chord ​BC​ subtends a right angle at the centre. The angle at a point on the circle is half the angle at the centre. If ​A​ lies on the major arc, ​\angle BAC = \frac{90^\circ}{2} = 45^\circ = \frac{\pi}{4}​. If ​A​ lies on the minor arc, the angle is ​180^\circ - 45^\circ = 135^\circ = \frac{3\pi}{4}​. Since the position of ​A​ is not given, both are possible. Answer: ​\pi/4​ or ​3\pi/4​.

promptLines: What are the coordinates of \(A\)?

options.D: Cannot be determined due to insufficient data

questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The only information about ​A​ is that it lies on the circle ​x^2 + y^2 = 100​, so that the triangle is inscribed. Every point of the circle other than ​B​ and ​C​ gives a valid triangle. In fact all three points in options (a), (b) and (c) lie on the circle: ​36 + 64 = 100​, ​36 + 64 = 100​ and ​50 + 50 = 100​. Nothing in the data picks one of them over the others. So ​A​ cannot be fixed. Answer: Cannot be determined due to insufficient data.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : \(ABCD\) is an isosceles trapezium and \(AB\) is parallel to \(DC\). Let \(A(2, 3)\), \(B(4, 3)\), \(C(5, 1)\) be the vertices.
What are the coordinates of vertex \(D\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

​AB​ joins ​(2, 3)​ and ​(4, 3)​, so it is horizontal. ​DC​ is parallel to it and passes through ​C(5, 1)​, so ​D = (d, 1)​. Isosceles means the slant sides are equal: ​AD = BC​. ​BC^2 = (5 - 4)^2 + (1 - 3)^2 = 5​. ​AD^2 = (d - 2)^2 + 4 = 5​ gives ​d = 1​ or ​d = 3​. With ​d = 3​, ​AD​ would be parallel to ​BC​ and the figure would be a parallelogram, not an isosceles trapezium. So ​d = 1​: the figure is then symmetric about the line ​x = 3​. Answer: ​(1, 1)​.

promptLines: What is the point of intersection of the diagonals of the trapezium?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

First find ​D​. ​DC​ is horizontal through ​C(5, 1)​, so ​D = (d, 1)​; equal slant sides ​AD = BC = \sqrt{5}​ give ​d = 1​ (the value ​d = 3​ makes a parallelogram). So ​D = (1, 1)​. The trapezium is symmetric about the line ​x = 3​, so the diagonals meet on ​x = 3​. Diagonal ​AC​ joins ​(2, 3)​ and ​(5, 1)​: slope ​= -\frac{2}{3}​, so ​y = 3 - \frac{2}{3}(x - 2)​. At ​x = 3​: ​y = 3 - \frac{2}{3} = \frac{7}{3}​. Check on ​BD​ from ​(4, 3)​ to ​(1, 1)​: ​y = 3 + \frac{2}{3}(3 - 4) = \frac{7}{3}​. Answer: ​(3, 7/3)​.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \(2x^2 + 2y^2 + 2z^2 + 3x + 3y + 3z - 6 = 0\) be a sphere.
What is the diameter of the sphere?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Divide by 2 to make the coefficients of the squares 1: ​x^2 + y^2 + z^2 + \frac{3}{2}x + \frac{3}{2}y + \frac{3}{2}z - 3 = 0​. Compare with ​x^2 + y^2 + z^2 + 2ux + 2vy + 2wz + d = 0​: ​u = v = w = \frac{3}{4}​, ​d = -3​. Radius ​= \sqrt{u^2 + v^2 + w^2 - d} = \sqrt{\frac{27}{16} + 3} = \sqrt{\frac{75}{16}} = \frac{5\sqrt{3}}{4}​. The diameter is twice this: ​\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}​. Option (a) is the radius, so take care. Answer: ​\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}​.

promptLines: The centre of the sphere lies on the plane
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Divide the equation by 2: ​x^2 + y^2 + z^2 + rac{3}{2}x + rac{3}{2}y + rac{3}{2}z - 3 = 0​. The centre is (minus half of each first-degree coefficient): ​\left(- rac{3}{4}, - rac{3}{4}, - rac{3}{4} ight)​. Put it in each plane. (a): ​- rac{9}{2} - 3 eq 0​. (b): ​-9 - 3 eq 0​. (c): ​-3 - 6 - 6 - 15 = -30 eq 0​. (d): ​-3 - 6 - 6 + 15 = 0​. Only (d) is satisfied. Answer: ​4x + 8y + 8z + 15 = 0​.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \(S\) be the line of intersection of two planes \(x + y + z = 1\) and \(2x + 3y - 4z = 8\).
Which of the following are the direction ratios of \(S\)?
questions.topicLabel: Line and plane in three dimensions
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The line of intersection lies in both planes, so it is perpendicular to both normals, ​(1, 1, 1)​ and ​(2, 3, -4)​. Its direction is their cross product: ​\begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & -4 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(-4 - 3) - \hat{j}(-4 - 2) + \hat{k}(3 - 2) = (-7, 6, 1)​. Check: ​(-7, 6, 1) \cdot (1, 1, 1) = 0​ and ​(-7, 6, 1) \cdot (2, 3, -4) = -14 + 18 - 4 = 0​. Answer: ​\langle -7, 6, 1 \rangle​.

promptLines: If \(\langle l, m, n \rangle\) are direction cosines of \(S\), then what is the value of \(43(l^2 - m^2 - n^2)\)?
questions.topicLabel: Points in space and direction cosines
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The direction ratios of ​S​ come from the cross product of the normals ​(1, 1, 1)​ and ​(2, 3, -4)​, which is ​(-7, 6, 1)​. Direction cosines are the ratios divided by their length: ​\sqrt{49 + 36 + 1} = \sqrt{86}​. So ​l^2 = \frac{49}{86}​, ​m^2 = \frac{36}{86}​, ​n^2 = \frac{1}{86}​. Then ​l^2 - m^2 - n^2 = \frac{49 - 36 - 1}{86} = \frac{12}{86} = \frac{6}{43}​. Multiply by 43: the value is 6. (The squares make the sign of the direction irrelevant.) Answer: 6.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \(L : x + y + z + 4 = 0 = 2x - y - z + 8\) be a line and \(P : x + 2y + 3z + 1 = 0\) be a plane.
What are the direction ratios of the line?
questions.topicLabel: Line and plane in three dimensions
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The line is the intersection of the planes ​x + y + z + 4 = 0​ and ​2x - y - z + 8 = 0​, so it is perpendicular to both normals ​(1, 1, 1)​ and ​(2, -1, -1)​. Cross product: ​\hat{i}(1 \cdot (-1) - 1 \cdot (-1)) - \hat{j}(1 \cdot (-1) - 1 \cdot 2) + \hat{k}(1 \cdot (-1) - 1 \cdot 2) = (0, 3, -3)​. Dividing by 3 gives ​(0, 1, -1)​. Another way: adding the two equations gives ​3x + 12 = 0​, so ​x = -4​ all along the line and the first ratio must be 0; then ​y + z = 0​. Answer: ​\langle 0, 1, -1 \rangle​.

promptLines: What is the point of intersection of \(L\) and \(P\)?
questions.topicLabel: Line and plane in three dimensions
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The point must satisfy all three equations. Add the two equations of ​L​: ​(x + y + z + 4) + (2x - y - z + 8) = 0​ gives ​3x + 12 = 0​, so ​x = -4​. Put this in the first: ​y + z = 0​, so ​z = -y​. Now use the plane ​P​: ​-4 + 2y + 3(-y) + 1 = 0​, so ​-y - 3 = 0​ and ​y = -3​, ​z = 3​. The point is ​(-4, -3, 3)​. Check in ​2x - y - z + 8​: ​-8 + 3 - 3 + 8 = 0​. Correct. Answer: ​(-4, -3, 3)​.

promptLines: Let \(z = [y]\) and \(y = [x] - x\), where \([\cdot]\) is the greatest integer function. If \(x\) is not an integer but positive, then what is the value of \(z\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

For any ​x​, ​x - [x]​ is the fractional part of ​x​. When ​x​ is not an integer, this fractional part lies strictly between 0 and 1. So ​y = [x] - x​ is the negative of it and lies strictly between ​-1​ and ​0​. The greatest integer not exceeding a number between ​-1​ and ​0​ is ​-1​. Hence ​z = [y] = -1​. Example: ​x = 2.3​ gives ​y = 2 - 2.3 = -0.3​ and ​[-0.3] = -1​. Answer: ​-1​.

promptLines: If \(f(x) = 4x + 1\) and \(g(x) = kx + 2\) such that \(f \circ g(x) = g \circ f(x)\), then what is the value of \(k\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Work out both composites. ​f \circ g(x) = f(kx + 2) = 4(kx + 2) + 1 = 4kx + 9​. ​g \circ f(x) = g(4x + 1) = k(4x + 1) + 2 = 4kx + k + 2​. The ​x​ terms already agree, so we need the constants to agree: ​9 = k + 2​, giving ​k = 7​. Answer: 7.

promptLines: What is the minimum value of the function \(f(x) = \log_{10}(x^2 + 2x + 11)\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

​\log_{10}​ is an increasing function, so ​f​ is smallest when the quantity inside is smallest. Complete the square: ​x^2 + 2x + 11 = (x + 1)^2 + 10​. A square is never negative, so the least value is 10, reached at ​x = -1​. Therefore the minimum of ​f​ is ​\log_{10}10 = 1​. Answer: 1.

promptLines: Which one of the following is correct regarding \(\lim_{x \to 3} \frac{|x - 3|}{x - 3}\)?

options.A: Limit exists and is equal to 1
options.B: Limit exists and is equal to 0
options.C: Limit exists and is equal to \(-1\)

questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Look at the two sides separately. For ​x > 3​, ​|x - 3| = x - 3​, so the fraction equals ​1​; the right-hand limit is ​1​. For ​x < 3​, ​|x - 3| = -(x - 3)​, so the fraction equals ​-1​; the left-hand limit is ​-1​. A limit exists only when the left-hand and right-hand limits are equal. Here ​1 \neq -1​. Answer: Limit does not exist.

promptLines: What is the maximum value of \(a\cos x + b\sin x + c\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Write ​a = r\cos\alpha​ and ​b = r\sin\alpha​ with ​r = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}​. Then ​a\cos x + b\sin x = r(\cos x\cos\alpha + \sin x\sin\alpha) = r\cos(x - \alpha)​. Since cosine lies between ​-1​ and ​1​, this part lies between ​-\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}​ and ​\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}​. Adding the constant ​c​ shifts everything by ​c​. So the maximum is ​\sqrt{a^2 + b^2} + c​ (note that ​c​ is outside the root). Answer: ​\sqrt{a^2 + b^2} + c​.

promptLines: If \(f(2x) = 4x^2 + 1\), then for how many real values of \(x\) will \(f(2x)\) be the GM of \(f(x)\) and \(f(4x)\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Since ​f(2x) = (2x)^2 + 1​, the rule is ​f(t) = t^2 + 1​. So ​f(x) = x^2 + 1​ and ​f(4x) = 16x^2 + 1​. The GM condition is ​[f(2x)]^2 = f(x) \cdot f(4x)​: ​(4x^2 + 1)^2 = (x^2 + 1)(16x^2 + 1)​. Expand: ​16x^4 + 8x^2 + 1 = 16x^4 + 17x^2 + 1​. This gives ​9x^2 = 0​, so ​x = 0​ only. At ​x = 0​ all three values are 1, and 1 is indeed the GM of 1 and 1. So there is exactly one real value. Answer: One.

promptLines: If \(f(x) = [x]^2 - 30[x] + 221 = 0\), where \([x]\) is the greatest integer function, then what is the sum of all integer solutions?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Put ​t = [x]​. The equation is ​t^2 - 30t + 221 = 0​. We need two numbers with sum 30 and product 221: they are 13 and 17, so ​(t - 13)(t - 17) = 0​ and ​[x] = 13​ or ​[x] = 17​. ​[x] = 13​ holds for ​13 \leq x < 14​, where the only integer is 13. ​[x] = 17​ holds for ​17 \leq x < 18​, where the only integer is 17. So the integer solutions are 13 and 17, and their sum is ​13 + 17 = 30​. Answer: 30.

promptLines: If \(f(x) = 9x - 8\sqrt{x}\) such that \(g(x) = f(x) - 1\), then which one of the following is correct?

options.B: \(g(x) = 0\) has only one real root which is an integer
options.C: \(g(x) = 0\) has two real roots which are integers
options.D: \(g(x) = 0\) has only one real root which is not an integer

questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

​g(x) = 9x - 8\sqrt{x} - 1​. Put ​t = \sqrt{x}​, remembering ​t \geq 0​. Then ​9t^2 - 8t - 1 = 0​, which factorises as ​(9t + 1)(t - 1) = 0​. So ​t = 1​ or ​t = -\frac{1}{9}​. A square root cannot be negative, so ​t = -\frac{1}{9}​ is rejected. ​t = 1​ gives ​x = 1​. Check: ​9 - 8 - 1 = 0​. (Note ​x = \frac{1}{81}​ fails: ​\frac{1}{9} - \frac{8}{9} - 1 \neq 0​.) So there is only one real root, ​x = 1​, an integer. Answer: option (b).

promptLines: What is \(\lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}} (\sec\theta - \tan\theta)\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Our working gives (b). Misprint in the paper: the limit is printed with x tending to pi/2 while the function is in theta. Solved taking theta tending to pi/2, which is clearly what is meant.

Take the variable as ​\theta \to \frac{\pi}{2}​. Both ​\sec\theta​ and ​\tan\theta​ become infinite there, so combine them first: ​\sec\theta - \tan\theta = \frac{1 - \sin\theta}{\cos\theta}​. Multiply top and bottom by ​(1 + \sin\theta)​: ​\frac{1 - \sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta(1 + \sin\theta)} = \frac{\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta(1 + \sin\theta)} = \frac{\cos\theta}{1 + \sin\theta}​. As ​\theta \to \frac{\pi}{2}​ this tends to ​\frac{0}{1 + 1} = 0​. Answer: 0.

promptLines: Let \(f(x)f(y) = f(xy)\) for all real \(x\), \(y\). If \(f(2) = 4\), then what is the value of \(f(1/2)\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Put ​x = 2​, ​y = 1​: ​f(2)f(1) = f(2)​, so ​4f(1) = 4​ and ​f(1) = 1​. Now put ​x = 2​, ​y = \frac{1}{2}​: ​f(2)f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = f(1) = 1​. So ​4f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 1​ and ​f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{4}​. This agrees with the natural example ​f(x) = x^2​, which satisfies the rule and has ​f(2) = 4​. Answer: 1/4.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \(f \circ g(x) = \cos^2\sqrt{x}\) and \(g \circ f(x) = |\cos x|\).
Which one of the following is \(f(x)\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Look at ​f \circ g(x) = \cos^2\sqrt{x}​. It suggests an inner function ​g(x) = \sqrt{x}​ and an outer function ​f(x) = \cos^2 x​, since then ​f(g(x)) = \cos^2(\sqrt{x})​. Test this pair on the second condition: ​g(f(x)) = \sqrt{\cos^2 x} = |\cos x|​, because the square root of a square is the modulus. Both conditions hold. With ​f(x) = \cos x​ instead, ​g(f(x)) = \sqrt{\cos x}​, which is not ​|\cos x|​. Answer: ​\cos^2 x​.

promptLines: Which one of the following is \(g(x)\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Try ​g(x) = \sqrt{x}​ together with ​f(x) = \cos^2 x​. Then ​f(g(x)) = \cos^2(\sqrt{x})​, which matches the first condition. And ​g(f(x)) = \sqrt{\cos^2 x} = |\cos x|​, which matches the second, because ​\sqrt{a^2} = |a|​. The other choices fail: for example ​g(x) = |x|​ would need ​f(|x|) = \cos^2\sqrt{x}​ and ​|f(x)| = |\cos x|​ together, which cannot both hold. Answer: ​\sqrt{x}​.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \(f(x) = [x]^2 - [x^2]\).
What is \(f(0 \cdot 999) + f(1 \cdot 001)\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Our working gives (b). The paper does not say so in the English text, but [x] is taken as the greatest integer function, as elsewhere in the paper.

Here ​[\,\cdot\,]​ is the greatest integer function. At ​x = 0.999​: ​[x] = 0​, and ​x^2 \approx 0.998​, so ​[x^2] = 0​. Thus ​f(0.999) = 0^2 - 0 = 0​. At ​x = 1.001​: ​[x] = 1​, and ​x^2 = 1.002001​, so ​[x^2] = 1​. Thus ​f(1.001) = 1^2 - 1 = 0​. The sum is ​0 + 0 = 0​. Answer: 0.

promptLines: Consider the following statements :
I. \(f(x)\) is continuous at \(x = 0\).
II. \(f(x)\) is continuous at \(x = 1\).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

At ​x = 0​: ​f(0) = 0 - 0 = 0​. Just to the right (​0 < x < 1​): ​[x] = 0​ and ​[x^2] = 0​, so ​f = 0​. Just to the left (​-1 < x < 0​): ​[x] = -1​, so ​[x]^2 = 1​, while ​x^2​ is between 0 and 1, so ​[x^2] = 0​; ​f = 1​. The left limit 1 differs from ​f(0) = 0​, so ​f​ is not continuous at 0. At ​x = 1​: ​f(1) = 1 - 1 = 0​. Just left of 1, ​f = 0 - 0 = 0​. Just right of 1 (​1 < x < \sqrt{2}​): ​[x] = 1​, ​[x^2] = 1​, ​f = 0​. All agree, so ​f​ is continuous at 1. Answer: II only.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \(f(x) = \cos 2x + x\) on \([-\pi/2, \pi/2]\).
What is the greatest value of \(f(x)\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

​f'(x) = -2\sin 2x + 1​. Setting it to zero: ​\sin 2x = \frac{1}{2}​. With ​2x​ in ​[-\pi, \pi]​, ​2x = \frac{\pi}{6}​ or ​\frac{5\pi}{6}​, so ​x = \frac{\pi}{12}​ or ​\frac{5\pi}{12}​. Compare values at these points and at the end points. ​f\left(\frac{\pi}{12}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{\pi}{12} \approx 1.13​. ​f\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right) = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{5\pi}{12} \approx 0.44​. ​f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = -1 + \frac{\pi}{2} \approx 0.57​. ​f\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = -1 - \frac{\pi}{2} \approx -2.57​. The greatest is at ​x = \frac{\pi}{12}​. Answer: ​\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{\pi}{12}​.

promptLines: What is the least value of \(f(x)\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

On a closed interval the least value occurs at a critical point or an end point. ​f'(x) = 1 - 2\sin 2x = 0​ gives ​\sin 2x = \frac{1}{2}​, so ​x = \frac{\pi}{12}​ or ​\frac{5\pi}{12}​. Values: ​f\left(\frac{\pi}{12}\right) \approx 1.13​, ​f\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right) = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{5\pi}{12} \approx 0.44​. End points: ​f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = \cos\pi + \frac{\pi}{2} = -1 + \frac{\pi}{2} \approx 0.57​ and ​f\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = \cos(-\pi) - \frac{\pi}{2} = -1 - \frac{\pi}{2} \approx -2.57​. The smallest is at the left end point. Answer: ​-\left(1 + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)​.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : The area bounded by the parabola \(y^2 = kx\) and the line \(x = k\), where \(k > 0\), is \(4/3\) square units.
What is the value of \(k\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The parabola ​y^2 = kx​ opens to the right and is symmetric about the x-axis. Its upper half is ​y = \sqrt{kx}​. The region between the curve and the line ​x = k​ has area ​2\int_0^k \sqrt{kx}\,dx = 2\sqrt{k} \cdot \frac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\Big|_0^k = \frac{4}{3}\sqrt{k} \cdot k^{3/2} = \frac{4}{3}k^2​. Set this equal to ​\frac{4}{3}​: ​k^2 = 1​, and since ​k > 0​, ​k = 1​. Answer: 1.

promptLines: What is the area of the parabola bounded by the latus rectum?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

First find ​k​: the area between ​y^2 = kx​ and ​x = k​ is ​2\int_0^k \sqrt{kx}\,dx = \frac{4}{3}k^2 = \frac{4}{3}​, so ​k = 1​ and the parabola is ​y^2 = x​. Compare with ​y^2 = 4ax​: ​4a = 1​, so ​a = \frac{1}{4}​ and the latus rectum is the line ​x = \frac{1}{4}​. Area cut off by it ​= 2\int_0^{1/4} \sqrt{x}\,dx = 2 \cdot \frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{3/2} = \frac{4}{3} \cdot \frac{1}{8} = \frac{1}{6}​. (This matches the standard result ​\frac{8a^2}{3}​.) Answer: 1/6 square unit.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \(y\,dx + (x - y^3)\,dy = 0\) be a differential equation.
What are the order and degree respectively of the differential equation?
questions.topicLabel: Differential equations: order, degree and formation
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Divide by ​dx​ to see the derivative: ​y + (x - y^3)\frac{dy}{dx} = 0​. The highest derivative present is the first derivative ​\frac{dy}{dx}​, so the order is 1. The degree is the power of that highest derivative once the equation is a polynomial in derivatives; here ​\frac{dy}{dx}​ appears to the power 1. The ​y^3​ is a power of ​y​, not of a derivative, so it does not affect the degree. Answer: 1 and 1.

promptLines: What is the solution of the differential equation?
questions.topicLabel: Solving differential equations; growth and decay
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Open the bracket: ​y\,dx + x\,dy - y^3\,dy = 0​. The first two terms together are exactly the differential of a product: ​y\,dx + x\,dy = d(xy)​. So ​d(xy) = y^3\,dy​. Integrate both sides: ​xy = \frac{y^4}{4} + C​. Multiply by 4: ​4xy - y^4 = c​. Check by differentiating: ​4y\,dx + 4x\,dy - 4y^3\,dy = 0​, which is 4 times the given equation. Answer: ​4xy - y^4 = c​.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \(f(x) = |x^2 - x - 2|\).
What is \(\int_0^2 f(x)\,dx\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Factorise: ​x^2 - x - 2 = (x - 2)(x + 1)​. Between ​x = -1​ and ​x = 2​ this is negative or zero, so on ​[0, 2]​ the modulus changes its sign: ​f(x) = -x^2 + x + 2​. Then ​\int_0^2 (-x^2 + x + 2)\,dx = \left[-\frac{x^3}{3} + \frac{x^2}{2} + 2x\right]_0^2 = -\frac{8}{3} + 2 + 4 = \frac{10}{3}​. Answer: 10/3.

promptLines: What is \(\int_1^3 f(x)\,dx\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

​x^2 - x - 2 = (x - 2)(x + 1)​ is negative on ​[1, 2)​ and positive on ​(2, 3]​, so split at ​x = 2​. On ​[1, 2]​: ​\int_1^2 (-x^2 + x + 2)\,dx = \left[-\frac{x^3}{3} + \frac{x^2}{2} + 2x\right]_1^2 = \frac{10}{3} - \frac{13}{6} = \frac{7}{6}​. On ​[2, 3]​: ​\int_2^3 (x^2 - x - 2)\,dx = \left[\frac{x^3}{3} - \frac{x^2}{2} - 2x\right]_2^3 = -\frac{3}{2} - \left(-\frac{10}{3}\right) = \frac{11}{6}​. Total ​= \frac{7}{6} + \frac{11}{6} = 3​. Answer: 3.

Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \(f(t) = \ln(t + \sqrt{1 + t^2})\) and \(g(t) = \tan(f(t))\).
Consider the following statements :
I. \(f(t)\) is an odd function.
II. \(g(t)\) is an odd function.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

A function is odd if ​f(-t) = -f(t)​. Here ​f(-t) = \ln(-t + \sqrt{1 + t^2})​. Multiply and divide by ​(t + \sqrt{1 + t^2})​: ​-t + \sqrt{1 + t^2} = \frac{(1 + t^2) - t^2}{t + \sqrt{1 + t^2}} = \frac{1}{t + \sqrt{1 + t^2}}​. So ​f(-t) = \ln\frac{1}{t + \sqrt{1 + t^2}} = -f(t)​. I is correct. Then ​g(-t) = \tan(f(-t)) = \tan(-f(t)) = -\tan(f(t)) = -g(t)​, since tan is odd. II is correct. Answer: Both I and II.

promptLines: What is \(\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} g(t)\,dt\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Our working gives (b). Intended answer is 0 by odd symmetry. Strictly, f(t) reaches pi/2 at t = sinh(pi/2), about 2.30, which is inside the interval, so tan(f(t)) is unbounded there and the integral is improper (it is 0 only as a principal value). The setter overlooked this.

First check whether ​g​ is odd. ​f(-t) = \ln(\sqrt{1 + t^2} - t) = \ln\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + t^2} + t} = -f(t)​, so ​f​ is odd. Then ​g(-t) = \tan(-f(t)) = -\tan(f(t)) = -g(t)​, so ​g​ is odd as well. For an odd function, the integral over an interval symmetric about zero is zero, because the area from ​-\pi​ to 0 cancels the area from 0 to ​\pi​: ​\int_{-a}^{a} g(t)\,dt = 0​. Answer: 0.

promptLines: Direction :

Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \(f : (-1, 1) \to R\) be a differentiable function with \(f(0) = -1\) and \(f'(0) = 1\). Let \(h(x) = f(2f(x) + 2)\) and \(g(x) = (h(x))^2\).
What is \(h'(0)\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Use the chain rule on ​h(x) = f(2f(x) + 2)​: ​h'(x) = f'(2f(x) + 2) \cdot 2f'(x)​. At ​x = 0​ the inner quantity is ​2f(0) + 2 = 2(-1) + 2 = 0​. So ​h'(0) = f'(0) \cdot 2f'(0) = 1 \times 2 \times 1 = 2​. Answer: 2.

promptLines: What is \(g'(0)\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

​g(x) = (h(x))^2​, so by the chain rule ​g'(x) = 2h(x)h'(x)​. We need ​h(0)​ and ​h'(0)​. ​h(0) = f(2f(0) + 2) = f(-2 + 2) = f(0) = -1​. ​h'(x) = f'(2f(x) + 2) \cdot 2f'(x)​, so ​h'(0) = f'(0) \cdot 2f'(0) = 2​. Therefore ​g'(0) = 2 \times (-1) \times 2 = -4​. Answer: ​-4​.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \(I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}\,dx\), where \(f(x) = \sin x\) and \(g(x) = \sin x + \cos x + 1\).
What is \(\int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{dx}{g(x)}\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Use the substitution ​t = \tan\frac{x}{2}​: ​\sin x = \frac{2t}{1 + t^2}​, ​\cos x = \frac{1 - t^2}{1 + t^2}​, ​dx = \frac{2\,dt}{1 + t^2}​. Then ​\sin x + \cos x + 1 = \frac{2t + 1 - t^2 + 1 + t^2}{1 + t^2} = \frac{2t + 2}{1 + t^2}​. So ​\frac{dx}{g(x)} = \frac{2\,dt}{2t + 2} = \frac{dt}{1 + t}​. Limits: ​x = 0​ gives ​t = 0​; ​x = \frac{\pi}{2}​ gives ​t = 1​. The integral is ​\int_0^1 \frac{dt}{1 + t} = \ln 2 - \ln 1 = \ln 2​. Answer: ​\ln 2​.

promptLines: What is \(I\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Use the property ​\int_0^a F(x)\,dx = \int_0^a F(a - x)\,dx​ with ​a = \frac{\pi}{2}​. It swaps sin and cos, so ​I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{\cos x}{\sin x + \cos x + 1}\,dx​ too. Add the two forms: ​2I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin x + \cos x}{\sin x + \cos x + 1}\,dx = \int_0^{\pi/2} \left(1 - \frac{1}{g(x)}\right)dx = \frac{\pi}{2} - \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{dx}{g(x)}​. With ​t = \tan\frac{x}{2}​ the last integral becomes ​\int_0^1 \frac{dt}{1 + t} = \ln 2​. So ​2I = \frac{\pi}{2} - \ln 2​ and ​I = \frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{\ln 2}{2}​. Answer: ​\frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{\ln 2}{2}​.

promptLines: Direction :
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow : Let \(2\int \frac{x^2 - 1}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}\,dx = U(x)V(x) - 3\ln\{U(x) + V(x)\} + c\)
What is \(|U^2(x) - V^2(x)|\) equal to?
questions.topicLabel: Integration: the idea and standard integrals
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Write ​x^2 - 1 = (x^2 + 1) - 2​. Then ​\int \frac{x^2 - 1}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}\,dx = \int \sqrt{x^2 + 1}\,dx - 2\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}​. Standard results: ​\int \sqrt{x^2 + 1}\,dx = \frac{x}{2}\sqrt{x^2 + 1} + \frac{1}{2}\ln(x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1})​ and ​\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}} = \ln(x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1})​. So the integral is ​\frac{x}{2}\sqrt{x^2 + 1} - \frac{3}{2}\ln(x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1})​, and twice it is ​x\sqrt{x^2 + 1} - 3\ln(x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1}) + c​. Comparing, ​U​ and ​V​ are ​x​ and ​\sqrt{x^2 + 1}​. Then ​|U^2 - V^2| = |x^2 - (x^2 + 1)| = 1​. Answer: 1.

promptLines: What is \(U(x)V(x)\) equal to?
questions.topicLabel: Integration: the idea and standard integrals
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Our working gives (a). ​x\sqrt{x^2+1}​ equals ​\sqrt{x^2+x^4}​ only for ​x \geq 0​; the options ignore the sign.

Write ​x^2 - 1 = (x^2 + 1) - 2​, so the integrand is ​\sqrt{x^2 + 1} - \frac{2}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}​. Using ​\int \sqrt{x^2 + 1}\,dx = \frac{x}{2}\sqrt{x^2 + 1} + \frac{1}{2}\ln(x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1})​ and ​\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}} = \ln(x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1})​, twice the integral is ​x\sqrt{x^2 + 1} - 3\ln(x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1}) + c​. So ​U(x)V(x) = x\sqrt{x^2 + 1}​. Taking ​x​ inside the root (for ​x \geq 0​): ​\sqrt{x^2(x^2 + 1)} = \sqrt{x^2 + x^4}​. Answer: ​\sqrt{x^2 + x^4}​.

promptLines: Let \(x - 3y + 4 = 0\) and \(2x - 7y + 8 = 0\) be two lines of regression computed from some bivariate data. If \(b_{yx}\) and \(b_{xy}\) are regression coefficients of lines of regression of \(y\) on \(x\) and \(x\) on \(y\) respectively, then what is the value of \(b_{xy} + 7b_{yx}\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

We must decide which line is ​y​ on ​x​. The test is that ​b_{yx} \cdot b_{xy} = r^2​ cannot exceed 1. Try the first line as ​y​ on ​x​: ​y = \frac{x}{3} + \frac{4}{3}​, ​b_{yx} = \frac{1}{3}​; the second as ​x​ on ​y​: ​x = \frac{7y}{2} - 4​, ​b_{xy} = \frac{7}{2}​. Product ​= \frac{7}{6} > 1​, not allowed. So swap: the first line is ​x​ on ​y​: ​x = 3y - 4​, ​b_{xy} = 3​; the second is ​y​ on ​x​: ​y = \frac{2x}{7} + \frac{8}{7}​, ​b_{yx} = \frac{2}{7}​. Product ​= \frac{6}{7} < 1​, fine. Then ​b_{xy} + 7b_{yx} = 3 + 2 = 5​. Answer: 5.

promptLines: The mean of \(n\) observations \(1, 4, 9, 16, \ldots, n^2\) is 130. What is the value of \(n\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The sum of the first ​n​ squares is ​\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}​. Dividing by ​n​, the mean is ​\frac{(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}​. Set this equal to 130: ​(n + 1)(2n + 1) = 780​. Try the options: ​n = 19​ gives ​20 \times 39 = 780​. It fits. (​n = 18​ gives ​19 \times 37 = 703​ and ​n = 20​ gives ​21 \times 41 = 861​.) Answer: 19.

promptLines: Three distinct natural numbers are chosen at random from 1 to 10. What is the probability that they are consecutive?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Total ways to choose 3 different numbers from 10: ​\binom{10}{3} = \frac{10 \times 9 \times 8}{6} = 120​. Favourable choices are sets of three consecutive numbers: ​\{1, 2, 3\}, \{2, 3, 4\}, \ldots, \{8, 9, 10\}​. The smallest number can be anything from 1 to 8, so there are 8 such sets. Probability ​= \frac{8}{120} = \frac{1}{15}​. Answer: 1/15.

promptLines: \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) are three mutually exclusive and exhaustive events associated with a random experiment. If \(3P(B) = 4P(A)\) and \(3P(C) = 2P(B)\), then what is \(P(A)\) equal to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Mutually exclusive and exhaustive events have probabilities adding to 1: ​P(A) + P(B) + P(C) = 1​. Let ​P(A) = a​. Then ​P(B) = \frac{4a}{3}​, and ​P(C) = \frac{2}{3}P(B) = \frac{8a}{9}​. So ​a + \frac{4a}{3} + \frac{8a}{9} = 1​. With denominator 9: ​\frac{9a + 12a + 8a}{9} = \frac{29a}{9} = 1​, giving ​a = \frac{9}{29}​. Check: ​P(B) = \frac{12}{29}​, ​P(C) = \frac{8}{29}​, total ​\frac{29}{29}​. Answer: 9/29.

promptLines: A die has two faces with number 4, three faces with number 5 and one face with number 6. If the die is rolled once, then what is the probability of getting 4 or 5?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The die has 6 equally likely faces. Two of them show 4 and three show 5, so ​2 + 3 = 5​ faces show a 4 or a 5. Probability ​= \frac{5}{6}​. Equivalently, the only face that fails is the single 6, so the probability is ​1 - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}​. Answer: 5/6.

promptLines: A box contains 2 black, 4 yellow and 6 white balls. Three balls are drawn in succession with replacement. What is the probability that all three are of the same colour?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

There are 12 balls. Because each ball is put back, every draw has the same chances: black ​\frac{2}{12} = \frac{1}{6}​, yellow ​\frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}​, white ​\frac{6}{12} = \frac{1}{2}​, and the draws are independent. All black: ​\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^3 = \frac{1}{216}​. All yellow: ​\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^3 = \frac{8}{216}​. All white: ​\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{27}{216}​. Add these exclusive cases: ​\frac{1 + 8 + 27}{216} = \frac{36}{216} = \frac{1}{6}​. Answer: 1/6.

promptLines: \(A\) can hit a target 5 times in 6 shots, \(B\) can hit 4 times in 5 shots and \(C\) can hit 3 times in 4 shots. What is the probability that \(A\) and \(C\) may hit but \(B\) may lose?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

​P(A \text{ hits}) = \frac{5}{6}​, ​P(B \text{ hits}) = \frac{4}{5}​ so ​P(B \text{ misses}) = 1 - \frac{4}{5} = \frac{1}{5}​, and ​P(C \text{ hits}) = \frac{3}{4}​. The three shooters act independently, so multiply: ​P(A \text{ hits}, B \text{ misses}, C \text{ hits}) = \frac{5}{6} \times \frac{1}{5} \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{15}{120} = \frac{1}{8}​. Answer: 1/8.

promptLines: The letters of the word ZOOLOGY are arranged in all possible ways. What is the probability that the consonants and vowels occur alternatively?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Our working gives (d). Y is counted as a consonant, as is usual in such questions.

ZOOLOGY has 7 letters: three O's (vowels) and four consonants Z, L, G, Y. Total arrangements, with O repeated three times: ​\frac{7!}{3!} = 840​. For alternation with 4 consonants and 3 vowels the pattern must be C V C V C V C. The four different consonants fill their four places in ​4! = 24​ ways. The three O's are identical, so they fill the vowel places in just 1 way. Favourable ​= 24​. Probability ​= \frac{24}{840} = \frac{1}{35}​. Answer: 1/35.

promptLines: A natural number \(x\) is chosen at random from the first 100 natural numbers. What is the probability that \(x^2 + x > 50\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

​x^2 + x = x(x + 1)​ increases as ​x​ increases, so find where it first exceeds 50. ​x = 6​: ​6 \times 7 = 42​, not more than 50. ​x = 7​: ​7 \times 8 = 56 > 50​. So the condition holds for ​x = 7, 8, \ldots, 100​ and fails for ​x = 1​ to ​6​. Favourable numbers: ​100 - 6 = 94​. Probability ​= \frac{94}{100} = \frac{47}{50}​. Answer: 47/50.

promptLines: What is the mean deviation of the first 10 natural numbers?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The numbers are ​1, 2, \ldots, 10​. Mean ​= \frac{55}{10} = 5.5​ (the median is also 5.5). Mean deviation is the average of the distances from the mean. The distances are ​4.5, 3.5, 2.5, 1.5, 0.5​ for ​1​ to ​5​, and the same five values again for ​6​ to ​10​. Their total is ​2(4.5 + 3.5 + 2.5 + 1.5 + 0.5) = 2 \times 12.5 = 25​. Mean deviation ​= \frac{25}{10} = 2.5​. Answer: 2.5.

promptLines: Let \(\sum_{i=1}^{9} x_i^2 = 855\). If \(M\) is the mean and \(\sigma\) is the standard deviation of \(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_9\), then what is the value of \(M^2 + \sigma^2\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

The variance formula is ​\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum x_i^2}{n} - M^2​ (mean of the squares minus the square of the mean). Move ​M^2​ to the other side: ​M^2 + \sigma^2 = \frac{\sum x_i^2}{n}​. Here ​n = 9​ and ​\sum x_i^2 = 855​. So ​M^2 + \sigma^2 = \frac{855}{9} = 95​. Answer: 95.

promptLines: The mean of the series \(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n\) is \(\bar{x}\). If \(x_n\) is replaced by \(k\), then what is the new mean?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Mean ​=​ sum divided by number of terms, so the original sum is ​n\bar{x}​. Replacing ​x_n​ by ​k​ removes ​x_n​ from the sum and adds ​k​: the new sum is ​n\bar{x} - x_n + k​. The number of terms is still ​n​. So the new mean is ​\frac{n\bar{x} - x_n + k}{n}​. Answer: ​\frac{n\bar{x} - x_n + k}{n}​.

promptLines: A fair coin is tossed till two heads occur in succession. What is the probability that the number of tosses required is less than 6?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

We need HH to appear for the first time at toss 2, 3, 4 or 5. Ending at toss 2: HH, probability ​\frac{1}{4}​. At toss 3: THH, ​\frac{1}{8}​. At toss 4: the last three tosses are THH and the first toss is free (TTHH, HTHH): ​\frac{2}{16}​. At toss 5: the last three are THH and the first two must not be HH (TT, TH, HT): ​\frac{3}{32}​. Add: ​\frac{8}{32} + \frac{4}{32} + \frac{4}{32} + \frac{3}{32} = \frac{19}{32}​. Check: of the 32 sequences of five tosses, 19 contain HH. Answer: 19/32.

promptLines: Urn \(A\) contains 2 white and 2 black balls while urn \(B\) contains 3 white and 2 black balls. One ball is transferred from urn \(A\) to urn \(B\) and then a ball is drawn out of urn \(B\). What is the probability that the ball is white?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Use the total probability rule over what was transferred. A white ball is transferred with probability ​\frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}​; urn ​B​ then has 4 white and 2 black, so ​P(\text{white}) = \frac{4}{6}​. A black ball is transferred with probability ​\frac{1}{2}​; urn ​B​ then has 3 white and 3 black, so ​P(\text{white}) = \frac{3}{6}​. Total: ​\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{6} + \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{6} = \frac{4}{12} + \frac{3}{12} = \frac{7}{12}​. Answer: 7/12.

promptLines: For two events \(A\) and \(B\), \(P(A) = P(A|B) = 0 \cdot 25\) and \(P(B|A) = 0 \cdot 5\). Which of the following are correct?
I. \(A\) and \(B\) are independent.
II. \(P(A^c \cup B^c) = 0 \cdot 875\)
III. \(P(A^c \cap B^c) = 0 \cdot 375\)
Select the answer using the code given below.
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

I: ​P(A|B) = P(A)​ means knowing ​B​ does not change the chance of ​A​, so ​A​ and ​B​ are independent. Correct. Then ​P(B) = P(B|A) = 0.5​ and ​P(A \cap B) = 0.25 \times 0.5 = 0.125​. II: by De Morgan, ​A^c \cup B^c = (A \cap B)^c​, so its probability is ​1 - 0.125 = 0.875​. Correct. III: ​A^c \cap B^c = (A \cup B)^c​. ​P(A \cup B) = 0.25 + 0.5 - 0.125 = 0.625​, so the probability is ​1 - 0.625 = 0.375​. Correct. Answer: I, II and III.

promptLines: Two perfect dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers on the faces is neither 9 nor 10?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

Two dice give ​6 \times 6 = 36​ equally likely outcomes. Sum 9: ​(3, 6), (4, 5), (5, 4), (6, 3)​, which is 4 outcomes. Sum 10: ​(4, 6), (5, 5), (6, 4)​, which is 3 outcomes. So 7 outcomes give a sum of 9 or 10. The rest, ​36 - 7 = 29​, give neither. Probability ​= \frac{29}{36}​. Answer: 29/36.

promptLines: The occurrence of a disease in an industry is such that the workers have 20% chance of suffering from it. What is the probability that out of 6 workers chosen at random, 4 or more will suffer from the disease?
questions.topicLabel: Random variables and the binomial distribution
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

This is a binomial distribution with ​n = 6​, ​p = \frac{1}{5}​, ​q = \frac{4}{5}​, and ​P(X = r) = \binom{6}{r}p^r q^{6-r}​. Every term has denominator ​5^6 = 15625​. ​P(4) = 15 \times 1 \times 16 = 240​ parts. ​P(5) = 6 \times 1 \times 4 = 24​ parts. ​P(6) = 1​ part. Total ​= \frac{240 + 24 + 1}{15625} = \frac{265}{15625}​. Divide top and bottom by 5: ​\frac{53}{3125}​. Answer: 53/3125.

promptLines: Three perfect dice are rolled. Under the condition that no two show the same face, what is the probability that one of the faces shown is an ace (one)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

This is a conditional probability, so count only outcomes with three different faces: ​6 \times 5 \times 4 = 120​. Among these, count those containing a 1. The 1 can be on any of the 3 dice; the other two dice then show two different numbers from the remaining five, in ​5 \times 4 = 20​ ways. That gives ​3 \times 20 = 60​. Probability ​= \frac{60}{120} = \frac{1}{2}​. Another way: the three faces are a random set of 3 out of 6 numbers, and a particular number is in it with chance ​\frac{3}{6}​. Answer: 1/2.

promptLines: Three perfect dice \(D_1\), \(D_2\) and \(D_3\) are rolled. Let \(x\), \(y\) and \(z\) represent the numbers on \(D_1\), \(D_2\) and \(D_3\) respectively. What is the number of possible outcomes such that \(x < y < z\)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

For ​x < y < z​ the three numbers must all be different. Pick any 3 different numbers from ​1​ to ​6​: this can be done in ​\binom{6}{3} = 20​ ways. Once the three numbers are picked there is exactly one way to give them to the dice so that ​x < y < z​: the smallest goes to ​D_1​, the middle one to ​D_2​ and the largest to ​D_3​. So the number of outcomes is 20. Answer: 20.

promptLines: In a binomial distribution, if the mean is 6 and the standard deviation is \(\sqrt{2}\), then what are the values of the parameters \(n\) and \(p\) respectively?
questions.topicLabel: Random variables and the binomial distribution
questions.solutionHtml:
Answer: (unknown)

For a binomial distribution, mean ​= np​ and variance ​= npq​, where ​q = 1 - p​. The variance is the square of the standard deviation: ​(\sqrt{2})^2 = 2​. So ​np = 6​ and ​npq = 2​. Divide: ​q = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}​, hence ​p = 1 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}​. Then ​n = \frac{6}{p} = 6 \times \frac{3}{2} = 9​. Check: ​9 \times \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{1}{3} = 2​. Answer: 9 and 2/3.
